Case reference: 2014005450.CaseDesc: On June 6, 1979, James Gordon Nevin left his home in Amherstburg, Ontario, for a two-week vacation to visit relatives. He had a grandson in Winnipeg, Manitoba and a son in Prince George, British Columbia. The relatives were not informed of his planned visit.   On June 14, 1979, the RCMP responded to a call and located his 1974 white/maroon Dodge Coronet in a ditch between Rocanville, Saskatchewan and St. Lazare, Manitoba. Investigative findings indicate that the vehicle has been at this location since June 8, 1979.  James' whereabouts are currently unknown and it is believed that he was last seen between 1:30 p.m. and 3:00 p.m. on June 8, 1979. Extensive land and air searches have been conducted, all with negative results. The possibility of foul play cannot be discounted.

Scar: Right Thumb, Skin graft scar on right or left thumb

The numbers visible on the surgical plates could not be traced to a specific individual, however, it was determined that the lot was released some time after May 25, 1994. A MacDonald’s name tag with the name "Raymond" was found in the sewer, which may or may not be related to this individual.

Teeth: Visible Missing, Teeth were stained, which suggests he may have been a smoker,  his upper central incisors were also missing
Fractured/Broken Bones: Left Hip, recent fracture of left hip

An extensive search of the area was conducted with negative results.

Frances Gazeley was last seen on the evening of December 7, 2021. She was last
seen in the Weyburn, Saskatchewan area but could also be in the Ceylon, Minton,

It was learned that neither of them was prepared to be out for this period of time. At some point, Denny and his friend had a difference of opinion on whether they should continue on their journey or not, and the two ended up separating. The last confirmed sighting of Denny was just south of the Kiskatinaw Bridge on Highway 97. Denny has some disabilities and it is recommended that he be under adult supervision.

Shoes: Black, Purple, green and white "Osiris" brand
Sweater: Grey, Dark grey hoodie with red "DGK" symbol

Case reference: 2014001434.CaseDesc: Mario Hudon was last seen on May 16, 1983, when he left his parents' home in Lévis, Quebec, on the south shore of Quebec City. Mario left some of his personal belongings at the residence.

Case reference: 2014005541.CaseDesc: On September 5, 2010, Shawn Smith was seen for the last time in Toronto, Ontario. On September 6, Shawn arrived in the Dominican Republic and was scheduled to return on September 12, but never returned home.

Case reference: 2014001731.CaseDesc: On August 5, 1987, Russell Atkinson was last seen boarding a Greyhound bus in Penticton, British Columbia. The bus was destined for Winnipeg, Manitoba.  Russell did not arrive in Winnipeg but his luggage was found on the bus.

Case reference: 2012020653.CaseDesc: Patsy Haysom was last seen on May 12, 2003, when she was dropped off at the rear of her residence by a friend.

Case reference: 2014002562.CaseDesc: Michael Megraw, from Minnesota, USA, had visited the Katamik Lake area in Manitoba with his brother to go fishing over the September Labour Day weekend in September 1992.  Michael had returned to the US, but he was reported missing just days later. His family indicated that he was last seen on September 11, 1992.  On October 3, 1992, the RCMP received a call regarding a truck that had not been moved from Katamik Lake since September 24th. Michael Megraw was identified as the registered owner.  It is believed that he returned to the lake between September 11 and 24, 1992. Michael has not been seen since.

Case reference: 2019070875.CaseDesc: On April 17, 2019, the remains of a woman were found in a crawl space of a triplex in Montreal, Québec.
